_comment: BlaiseGuard configuration for the Blaise compiler project itself.
Discovered automatically by walking up from the analysed path; an
explicit --config overrides it.  The SAMPLE config in
tools/blaise-guard/ deliberately mirrors the built-in defaults and is
what a new user copies -- do not tune that one for this codebase.
Thresholds below are measured against compiler/ and stdlib/, not
guessed.  Where a rule is relaxed the reason is recorded, so a future
reader can tell a deliberate trade-off from an unexamined default.

rules._BL-1001: 120 is the house limit and the code already respects it (41 hits).
_BL-1002: Raised 15 -> 60.  At 15 the compiler reports 1114 findings, which is a
description of the codebase rather than a defect list: the backends and
the semantic pass are built from long, flat dispatch routines that are
clearer whole than split.  60 keeps the genuinely oversized ones visible.
_BL-1003: Raised 3 -> 6.  1211 findings at depth 3, concentrated in codegen
over an instruction or node kind is the natural shape there.
rules._BL-1004: Off by default upstream: closures and shadowing keep it heuristic.
_BL-2001: Demoted to info.  3261 findings, and the top files are TESTS, where an
explicit Free is often deliberate (exercising teardown, or a non-ARC
fixture).  Worth reading, not worth failing a build over yet.
_BL-2004: Kept ON at info.  86 findings and they are GENUINE -- Ord(S[i]) has been
observed to miscompile under the self-hosted native stage (CLAUDE.md).
The bulk conversion to OrdAt currently segfaults the built compiler
rather than suppressed: the rule is right, the migration is blocked.
_BL-3001: minTokens raised 30 -> 120.  At 30 the compiler reports 6855 findings.
That is real duplication -- the known codegen-duplication problem tracked
in docs/future-improvements.adoc -- but at that threshold it drowns every
other rule. 120 surfaces only substantial clones.
